Technical report · measurement · preregistered

When a certificate is worth running — measured as a decision, not argued

A certificate's width was expected to warn before the certificate refused: the prediction registered in advance, in a file committed before any harness byte, was that the enclosure radius rises smoothly, over orders of magnitude, into the pitchfork. The registered advance warning did not exist: the certified radius is flat at about 6.8e-15 all the way into the pitchfork. The reason is structural, and it runs in two directions.

The certificate detects the boundary only when the boundary breaks the certificate's own proposition. The reason generalises to the instrument rather than to the boundary: this family's refusal channel is a binary interiority predicate and therefore carries no margin that could warn, while a channel whose margin is the radius's own denominator cannot help but warn — a folklore consequence of the radii polynomial, not a finding of ours. The consequence is what the rest of this page prices as a decision: three policies race on a public mean-field-game kernel, across the pitchfork where the constant equilibrium stops being unique. DEFAULT trusts a small residual — the documented practice. CERTIFIED trusts a closed enclosure. CERTIFIED-WIDE trusts a closed enclosure only when its proposition matches the decision being taken. The scoring is a closed-form threshold, no solver and no interval; the cost model is one ratio — what being wrong must cost, relative to refusing, before the cautious policy wins.

1 · The trap, in one paragraph

On one side of the pitchfork (the closed-form threshold c* = −σ²(2π)², corroborated on the page's own data by the kernel's determinant changing sign between c = -9.82 and -9.87), the constant equilibrium is the only one, and every policy agrees: 70 slack-side instances, 0 wrong, nothing to buy. Past it, the constant branch is still a genuine solution — the Newton solve lands on it with residual exactly zero — but it is no longer the only one. The default's residual past the boundary is exactly zero — the wrongness is not in the answer but in the decision proposition, which no residual of any size can see.

2 · What the certificate does there, and it is worse than refusing

The enclosure does not refuse past the boundary. It closes, correctly: existence and local uniqueness in a ball both hold for the constant branch. It closed on all 55 far-side instances — and the decision taken on its green light was wrong all 55 times, because the decision needed global uniqueness and the certificate never promised it. The prediction the family existed for held, stronger than registered: every far-side closure is a truthful certificate of local uniqueness, every far-side commit is adjudicated wrong, and the widened policy refuses 55 of 55, commits 0 wrong, at break-even 1.00.

The certificate detects the boundary only when the boundary breaks the certificate's own proposition. The ledger already holds the same lesson in its negative form: an earlier enclosure that closed — every instance certified, every control green — and was refused anyway, because the certified proposition was not the claimed one. This page is that refusal measured forward as policy arithmetic.

The repair is not a better enclosure — the enclosure was flawless. CERTIFIED-WIDE adds the missing clause to the proposition: commit only if a deliberate second-branch probe finds no rival solution. That policy refuses exactly the 55 dangerous instances and commits every safe one, which is what break-even 1.00 means: it wins the moment being wrong costs more than asking again.

3 · The scorecard, failures first

Every measurement behind this page was preregistered in a file committed alone, before its harness existed — and a preregistration written after the code is a description, not a prediction. Two of the five registered predictions failed, and they are the two a salesman would have wanted:

registeredoutcome
a refusal window exists around the singularityFALSIFIED — closed 125 of 125; any window is narrower than the 0.05 grid
the radius warns on approachFALSIFIED — flat: 3.877e-320 to 6.856e-15 across the whole slack side
slack side: certificate buys nothingheld — 70 instances, 0 wrong, break-even infinite
far side: closed certificate, wrong decision; widened proposition recoversheld, stronger — 55/55 vs 0/55
closed-form threshold agrees with the kernel's Jacobianheld — sign flip brackets c*

The registered refusal window did not exist: the enclosure closed on 125 of 125 grid points, including 0.05 from the singularity — a falsified prediction, reported in the same table as the ones that held.

The same test, run on an earlier law of this unit

2026-08-07 — the same discipline was turned on a law this unit had already recorded, and the law did not survive it. On the two withheld families, that law stated that the certificate's width-like output is non-increasing into its own refusal boundary; its pass/fail thresholds were transcribed from a preregistration committed before that harness existed, and it had reached the rung the ledger calls numerically supported. This shop's adversary then killed it: the width rises at consecutive certified grid points inside the law's own declared approach window, in both couplings, each rise clear of the arithmetic's own derived floor. The kill was hardened before it was accepted — it persists under a 10× finer step around the witness and under a 100× tighter cap on the enclosure radius with double the round budget, and a rise invariant under a 10× grid refinement and a 100× tighter solver cap is not a discretisation artifact — then re-run independently and reproduced byte-identical. It was re-measured in the direction that costs something: every clause the law's own falsifier actually evaluates still reproduces and does not fire, so what died is the statement's literal monotonicity word, not the flatness-then-refusal behaviour underneath it. The record was narrowed to exactly the word that failed rather than retracted, its status set to refuted, and the history entry appended rather than the original edited.

4 · Whether you get a warning is a choice you already made

The flat radius above is not a special misfortune of this family. A follow-up experiment, preregistered the same way, ran a 2×2: two boundaries (a binding constraint in a dispatch problem; this pitchfork) × two channels (the instrument's own; a constructed margin).

boundarychannel as constructedmargin channel
binding constraintsilent (a bit cannot warn)warns — slack decays monotonically, ratio 63, zero crossing AT the binding onset (R̄ = 2.85)
pitchforksilent (width flat within ×1.085)warns — invertibility margin falls 1.48 orders into the sign flip

The 2×2 held in all four cells: the same complementarity boundary is silent through a bit and loud through a slack margin; the same degeneracy boundary is silent through an exact-candidate width and loud through an invertibility margin.

A certificate warns exactly when the quantity it exposes has the boundary in its denominator. If you want warning, put a margin in the channel; if your channel is a bit, you have chosen not to be warned — at any boundary.

5 · What the literature already owns, stated before a referee has to

A literature gate ruled the width-grows-near-degeneracy observation FOLKLORE — the certified radius is the smaller root of a quadratic whose linear coefficient is the contraction margin, so growth and refusal are one event — and that ruling binds this page: no cell of the warning table is claimed as a finding. The general form of the no-warning statement is unwritable: active-set prediction in advance, with conditioning controlling how early, is a published positive result (Cartis & Yan, arXiv:1404.6770). Only the instrument-scoped version survives, and that is the only version on this page. The adjacent prior art was fetched and is cited bibliographically: vacuity-adjacent desingularization near bifurcations (van den Berg, Lessard & Queirolo, arXiv:2006.13373), certified bifurcation detection by interval analysis (arXiv:2608.07119), and cusp-bifurcation proofs (Lessard & Pugliese, arXiv:2404.00535). None states the decision comparison measured here; that absence is a documented search, not a proof of novelty, and it is recorded as such in the unit's literature files.

6 · Scope, stated

Not claimed

Any cell of the warning table as a finding (each is folklore or standard practice); any statement about certificates in general (one kernel, one grid, V ≡ 0 — and the exactness of the trivial branch is a property of that choice); a refusal window's nonexistence (the falsification is resolution-bounded); any minted certificate — No certificate is minted by this work: the family ships a measured comparison, and the ledger's own rules block a CERT without a cross-language second basis, which this family deliberately does not carry.

Claimed, and falsifiable

On this public family, with wrongness decided by a closed form the page states: the residual-trusting default and the enclosure-trusting policy commit 55 and 55 wrong decisions of 55 past the boundary, the proposition-matched policy commits 0 at break-even 1.00, and the warning behaviour of every channel measured follows its construction. Every number regenerates from two committed goldens whose batteries carry red controls.

Carlos Toledo builds computer-assisted proofs and the checks that keep them honest. This page asks the buyer's question of his own product — when is the certificate worth running? — and reports the region where the honest answer is "it is not", the region where it is worth everything, and the case where a flawless certificate green-lights a wrong decision because its proposition was never the one being decided.

Built on the open-source eqcert certification kernel (MIT). Get in touch.
